item.title: The Davis Bookworms — Sun Aug 30, 1:30 PM — Nashoba Wines
item.description:

item.title: August Open Mic & Music Trivia — Sun Aug 30, 6:00 PM — The Melon Ball – Watermelon Music
item.description:
Whether you’re looking for a venue to share your own talents or just looking to enjoy hearing (and seeing) some local performers, we invite you to this free monthly event. We provide the sound, stage and lights – the rest is up to you. Play us your favorite song, tell us some jokes, act out a scene from your favorite play with friends. We will continue to feature our Music Trivia contest throughout the evening in between acts. The winner will receive a $20 Watermelon Music gift card! We ask that each performance be suitable for an all-ages venue, and that you arrive on time and stay until the end to support your fellow performers. FREE!!! Doors open/sign-ups @ 5:30. First act @ 6:00. Please help support the Watermelon Music with your purchase of a drink or a snack at Open Mic! Non-alcoholic drinks and pre-packaged snacks are available for sale at The Melon Ball. (Cash or Venmo only) We hope to see you there!
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Intermediate Watercolor with Misuk Goltz — Tue Sep 1, 10:00 AM — Pence Gallery
item.description:
Intermediate Watercolor with Misuk Goltz Tuesdays, 10 AM – 12 PM | September 1, 8, 15, 22, 29 $170 Members, $190 Non-Members (Materials not included) This 5-week workshop with Misuk Goltz will focus on using your brushes to their full potential and practicing diverse hand motions to achieve painterly, expressive watercolor paintings. Students will learn how to distribute different values to create balanced and sophisticated artwork while painting various subjects. Please note that this class is intended for participants who have previous experience with watercolor techniques and color blending. The use of high-quality watercolor materials is strongly recommended to achieve the best results. Register here: https://pencegallery.org/education/programs/workshops-and-classes/ Any questions? Email pencegallery@gmail.com.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Human Relations Commission Meetings — Thu Nov 26, 6:30 PM — City Hall Community Chambers
item.description:
The Davis Human Relations Commission (HRC) meetings aim to promote mutual respect, understanding, justice, and advancing the human rights of all people. The Human Relations Commission meets on the fourth Thursday of each month at 6:30 p.m. The Commission takes a recess in July (no meeting in July).
Meetings take place in the Community Chambers at City Hall, 23 Russell Boulevard. For more information on meetings, membership, resolutions, and more, visit the Human Relations Commission site.
The HRC makes recommendations around equity and discrimination in the City, and supports the City in preventing and addressing discrimination while promoting diversity, equality, and justice relevant to the goals and policies of the City Council.
To contact or send emails to the commission, email: HRC@cityofdavis.org
Source: Hate-Free Together

The exhibition includes works by artists from around the country in a variety of mediums. JUROR’S STATEMENT The Axis Gallery received 658 submissions to an open call, and I could have selected five exhibitions instead of one without feeling professionally compromised. Narrowing such a high- quality profusion down to a single hang was a real challenge. Whereas traditional thematic trawls tend to be self-limiting, open calls like this one afford the juror no circumscribing guidance – only that of quality on the terms artists set for themselves. item.title: Weekly Game Night at Blue Note — Wed Sep 16, 5:00 PM
item.description:
Yolo County Board Game Gathering Update 8/14/25: **We're still active**, but we primarily use Discord to chat and plan events. (See group description for invite link.)
We still meet every Wednesday for board games at Blue Note Brewing Company. We'll have a handful of tables reserved near the back; just look for the pile of board games.
People usually start arriving around 5pm, and games start whenever people are ready. Blue Note closes at 9pm, and although we have a 5-10 minute grace period there, you should be in the process of final scoring by 9, or else pack it up and play again another day.
Game night is open to all ages! Blue Note is a brewery, not a bar, so there's no restriction against minors. In addition to their crafted-in-house beer selection, water and sodas are available.
You're not required to buy anything in order to join us, but we do encourage you to support local businesses. Blue Note's chef team makes a mean pizza, and there are other nearby downtown restaurants

item.title: Davis Farmers Market — Sat Aug 29, 8:00 AM — Central Park
item.description:
Year-round at Central Park in downtown Davis, thousands gather each week to shop for what is grown, raised, and made locally at our markets. We are dedicated to bringing farmers right to your table, so we stay open rain or shine. Walk rows of stalls lined with an array of fruits and vegetables, including certified organic produce, choice meats, chicken, seafood, wine, local eggs and honey. Choose from a variety of fresh-baked goods, plants, flowers and gifts. Enjoy a picnic from one of our many food stands, made from market ingredients. See the vendor list here: https://www.davisfarmersmarket.org/our-sellers/ Farmers Market Hours Central Park: Saturdays 8a–1p (year-round), and Wednesdays 3p–6p (September through March); 4p–8p (April through August) UC Davis – North Quad: Wednesdays 10a–1:30p (fall and spring quarters) Sutter Davis Hospital: Thursdays 10a–1p (May through September) Sutter Medical Center, Sacramento: Thursdays 2:30p–5:30p
Source: The Dirt
